::: {#exm-prior}
#### A uniform prior for a probability

Let $\pi$ be the probability that a randomly chosen adult in some population smokes.
Before collecting any data,
an analyst who considers every value of $\pi$ in $(0, 1)$ equally plausible
could use the uniform prior

$$\p(\pi) = 1, \quad 0 < \pi < 1.$$

Under this prior,
the prior probability that fewer than 10% of adults smoke is
$\Pr(\pi < 0.1) = \int_0^{0.1} 1 \, d\pi = 0.1$.
:::
